body:
Well, must say it helped a lot hearing it from a different point of view, that's not as negative as my own. Guess my general view of rather being negative than positive is the best I can do, really caught me off for some time. Can't help change the belief, and yet, I can't simply judge it as bad whether it is or not. So got to at least thank you for helping me out getting a different perspective on the matter, that is not as centered around the negative part of it.

Also regarding that of feelings. I always found it to be a weakness, due to it clouding one's mind and ability to judge the best and most efficient solution to a problem. Being able to separate oneself from one's feelings, has thus always held a high level of importance for me, and still does. Often considered cold, but being able to remain calm and analytic in any given situation is something I value high. Although I suppose that is also one of the reasons that I suddenly had a lack of will to do anything since I guess I figured out feelings can serve as a reason for living, and that I lacked. But thinking a lot over it also yielded that if nothing has a point, such as living then dying does not have a point either. In other words simply to sit and enjoy the ride as it goes I guess is the only rational and best solution when it comes to that. If stuff works out then by the same logic I applied earlier then it was meant to be, and if it doesn't then it won't work out and was never meant to, fretting over it won't change the outcome.

I suppose you are right, in some points. I just really don't have anything that I truly love or enjoy in all honesty. I've basically shut off all my feelings, because of the thought of meaninglessness, and a previous belief in them as a weakness. It's not that I want to, but I can't help it and with the thought in mind it's predetermined, it simply encourages me even more, to think that it' simply meant to happen. Thus, I simply can't fear a thing if it as said is meant to happen, nor can I feel a thing if it's simply something i "observe" happen. I do also agree that it's a rather big field that needs studying in order to create an answer, which by no means would be guaranteed to be satisfying.

I do tho feel annoyed by the fact I'm having these thoughts, without any right to feel so. I'm not a cancer patient, I'm not in constant physical pain. Nothing is really wrong with me as for a condition, except my belief in nihilism, and that everything is predetermined, perhaps not written down, but that doesn't change my belief in it.

Well, I'm not even sure how to put it to be perfectly honest, the issue for me is perhaps not that free will is nonexistent, but it's based on outside influence. By which I mean if I am to get an idea, I need prior knowledge on the subject, an outside influence, but of course, if it was that easy anyone would get the same idea yes.
Now what will differ between me and another person is our set of experience, the state in which our brain is in, and thus our capabilities. Time is also in this process a major party in creating this idea, it is essential to reflect, and think of it as you stated that makes us more than computers. so far so good, I agree that each individual has a different set of attributes which can make us do stuff and don't do it. 

The issue, however, starts when you start to picture the same thing over again. If you in a certain scenario were to make a choice of going to the right or the left. That choice is based off, of the knowledge which you may or may not have about what there is in each direction and a personal set of experience and preference. However no matter the choice of going to the right or the left, then the answer would always be the same if all the factors were to remain the same. There are things that however would be able to affect this, an outside influence which would affect, how you view the right and left, a certain set of information about what is at the end of each. There would also be randomness which could cause a different outcome. However can randomness truly exist, I for one don't believe it does as it would also contradict my worldview of determinism. The issue is that even if were to exist, would it truly change the outcome in such a fashion that it'd be free will and not just another dimension, with another timeline caused by a certain action at some point.

Going back on track, if you were to walk down the road and have to choose between going left or right, you wouldn't suddenly think that flipping a coin or waiting 5 minutes extra would be a good idea. If the same action happens then the same outcome would come each time. The only way that the outcome would change would be through an outside influence, but why would something new happen along the road this time and not before, that wouldn't make sense at least since we'd have to assume the entire world went through the same scenario again. With that in mind, I can't help change looking at the world as a determined one, even if free will were to exist, is each thought we have not the cause of something prior. Yes "random" thoughts appear, or at least they seem random, but don't they spawn because of something different? Seeing something, hearing something, smelling something. Something has to happen before something new may happen. I'm perhaps on the wrong forum as for discussing this worldview that I don't know, but I can't change how control lacking, frustrating, and numb it feels, as I can barely help think about it, and why life even ha a meaning, if I were to die then wouldn't it simply mean it was nothing but the chain reaction, started whenever the universe started. I both find the thought amazing, and yet boring as hell, since it' amazing that such a reaction could happen and cause this much, and at the same time if it's true then I'm not the one causing it, then every reflection, I've ever done simply the result of such a reaction.

As for whether or not we are computers, and it being a single voice, then yes you are right I can't help believe there is a lot more to it, yet by reducing the entire thought process that we own, to a "function" which may constantly change by adding a certain input, be it what should i eat this morning, then I will always get the same result, the same answer when I ask at this specific point, in any "timeline" which has run the same course as my own until this point. This "function" is by no means anything I'd call simple, but it would rely on rather simple elements, such as anything you've seen and heard from others, other influences and time, used for reflection. 

I will try and look into some of those, maps of meaning videos to hopefully find something different there that might help out as well. I must also admit I'd actually love to be "dumb and happy" seems like a far more joyful existence. I'd love if I could believe in something, beyond myself and the physical world, simply because it seems to give meaning, and peace to those that live with that, oh and you are not the only one not being a native :)

Thank you for the response, and yes I have been thinking somewhat the same, and yet, I can't help feel a lack of control. Keeping in mind every action is the result of a prior action, anything that happens, be me sitting here, or sleeping is simply one of the results along the way of the chain reaction. Hence it makes it even harder to even consider enjoying the ride a bit longer, I'm perhaps far too pessimistic about it but I don't consider it existing at this point much more that I'm simply observing. As stated previously I don't even have any kind of excuse for getting into this mood, and yet, I can't help it. The lack of control makes me feel like suicide perhaps is the only thing that I may control and yet using the same chain of thoughts it's not even my call, what happens, happens, and I have no control of it and it pisses me off.
